newsitem.title: INDIA: Explosives experts investigate India blast site.
newsitem.headline: Explosives experts investigate India blast site.

text.p: Explosives experts on Friday began sifting through debris at the site in India's western state of Maharashtra where 17 people died when two vehicles carrying gelatine exploded, police said.
"I think it was an accident," Deputy Superintendent of Police Vijay Chavan told Reuters from Satara, about 300 km (190 miles) southeast of Bombay.
He said the explosions on Thursday evening, occurred when two vehicles carrying gelatine, used in mining and construction, were being unloaded outside a warehouse.
Nine bodies have been identified, he said, adding the owner of the vehicles was among the dead.
He said three people were in serious condition with 78 percent burns. A total of 38 people were injured in the blast, of whom 10 with minor injuries had already left hospital.
"One or maybe both (vehicles) had electric detonators and gelatine sticks," he said. "There was first a small muffled explosion followed by a second big blast."
Most of the casualties were among people living in the neighbourhood, Chavan said. Between 30 and 40 houses had been damaged by the blasts, he said.
The dead included two children, eight men and seven women, he said.
